## Q1

```{r}
birthday_sim = function(n) {

  if (!is.numeric(n) || n < 1) {
    stop("n_room should be a positive number")
  }

  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE)

  repeated_bday = length(unique(birthdays)) < n

  repeated_bday
}
```

```{r}
birthday_sim_df =
  expand_grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |>
  mutate(res = map_lgl(group_size, birthday_sim)) |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarize(prob = mean(res))

birthday_sim_df
```
Plot
```{r}
birthday_sim_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = prob)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Probability that at Least Two People Share a Birthday",
    x = "Group Size",
    y = "Probability of a Shared Birthday"
  )
```
Plotting the probability of sharing the same birthday as a function of group size is a signmoidal curve. Generally the probability of sharing a birthday increases as group size increases peaking at almost 1 or 100% when group size is 50.
